newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada farm census shows C$6.2 bln in '95 upgrades.
newsitem.headline: Canada farm census shows C$6.2 bln in '95 upgrades.

text.p: Almost half of Canada's farms spent C$6.2 billion in 1995 on capital improvements, Statistics Canada's 1996 farm census data showed Wednesday.
The census was taken on May 14, 1996 and results were released a year later.
Forty eight percent of farms, 132,727 out of 276,548, reported spending C$6.2 billion on new machines, new land, used equipment and farm buildings.
The total value of farm capital in Canada was C$156.5 billion. The figure includes land, buildings, equipment, livestock and poultry, Statistics Canada said.
